input.source: user-provided lawful dump, kept outside git

X0.note: User-provided external retail XEX hash and title identity verified; no game binary or assets are tracked

X1.note: SDK v0.10.0 is pinned; eighteen live-memory-derived function entries have focused static regressions. ReXGlue codegen and Linux AMD64 build now accept the 68-byte 0x82341198 dispatcher; its runtime execution and the broader PPC/import/lowering report remain open. A new exact-XEX disassembly record pins the eight-byte 0x82BA27C0 r3-adjusting tail thunk to 0x82BA2840; its ReXGlue override and generated registration are recorded, while runtime audio-failure reproduction is still pending.

X2.note: The plugin-enabled Linux AMD64 probe verified the retail VdEnableRingBufferRPtrWriteBack call with physical address 0x17AF403C and block-size log2 6. The GPU worker advanced the big-endian readback at descriptor+0x3C through values 25, 49, and 73; exact-XEX helper 0x823B2920 reads that +0x3C field. Earlier pristine probes watched the distinct descriptor+0x00 word, object+0x2ABD predicate, current KTHREAD+0x58 and object+13432; helper 0x823B33A0 was not entered, and the timeout helper 0x823BA9C8 traps when object+13432 is null. The 2026-10-24 exact-XEX Linux/GDB follow-up confirms source-0 retail callback 0x823B37B8 and 3,231 writes toggling the watched predicate byte between 0x04 and 0x14 via 0x823A4E48/0x823A4908. A separate 20-second Linux/GDB run with the recorded host executable/runtime/plugin hashes logged at least three source-0 callbacks entering 0x823A4640. Four sampled deferred-handler entries had queue read/write indexes 0/0 and a zero first record. Six sampled software-queue helper entries observed predicate values 0x00 then 0x14; retail predicate 0x823A0310 tests mask 0x02, clear in those samples. A new controlled Linux/GDB run sampled twelve source-0 callbacks and twelve consumer entries on object 0xB7365F00; every sampled read/write index remained 0/0, while candidate queue writer 0x823A4758 had no breakpoint hits. The observed callback stack originates in ReXGlue's SetupGuestGpu interrupt-dispatch lambda. This narrows the missing event to queue production/registration; it does not identify the cause or prove frontend progress. A separate retail GDB trace saw two calls to IoDismountVolumeByFileHandle with handle 0xF800003C from 0x827061E0; its caller ignores the return and continues to NtClose, and the same run proceeded to guest PM4/Vulkan submission. This does not establish the API's general unmount semantics. The earlier retained Linux log and descriptor+0 watch did not establish the EVENT_WRITE_SHD destination; a later plugin-enabled run (evidence/xbox360_event_write_ring_head_20261024.json) records per-packet writes to guest destination 0x17AF4000 and head-word progression 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 0xB, 0xD, 0xF, corresponding to the previously identified descriptor backing at 0xB7AF4000. This resolves the destination observation but not software-queue completion or the missing predicate bit 0x02 producer. A controlled SDL/uinput run (evidence/xbox360_linux_xam_input_routing_20261024.json) confirms Start and A states reach retail XamInputGetState user 0; inputs did not advance the frontend. The guest wait cause and menu progress remain open. Before the latest controlled launches, unused ReXGlue xenia_memory_* shared-memory objects consumed 4.7 GiB of /dev/shm; unreferenced current-user objects were removed before subsequent runs. In the exact 30-second run, two relative shader-cache directory opens failed with no VFS device 205 ms after the first readback; they do not explain that first black frame, and later shader-cache effects remain unknown. The 60-second exact Linux/GDB follow-up sampled 27 entries of retail helper 0x823B33A0 through call index 1500: software queue tail object+0x2A9C rose from 3 to 3003, while global 0x831B3820 remained 0 and the 1,624 observed predicate-byte writes were only 0x04/0x14. Static XEX code sets mask 0x02 only when VdIsHSIOTrainingSucceeded reports false; both the pinned ReXGlue stub and upstream Xenia return success (1), so this is expected retail gating and should not be forced. The separate software-queue consumer/head and predicate-bit 0x02 producer remain unresolved. A new 45-second exact-XEX Linux/GDB probe confirms startup registers callback 0x82649B68 on object 0xB7365F00 through 0x823A5730; the full retail leaf setter at 0x823A5730 stores r4 to r3+0x409C, matching the deferred producer callback slot. This identifies the stored field for those observed setter arguments but does not establish a producer hit or callback invocation. Source-0 interrupt delivery enters 0x823A4640, where eight sampled queue read/write index pairs remain 0/0. Candidate producer 0x823A4758 and the registered callback body were not hit. The producer and callback remain dynamically unobserved; frontend progress is unresolved. Static disassembly of 0x823B37B8 shows its source-0 branch calls 0x823A4640 only when separate address 0x7FC86544 has bit 0 set; this gate is distinct from object+0x2ABD bit 0x02 and global 0x831B3820. A new independent 60-second exact-XEX Linux/GDB trace on the current selected plugin artifact (SHA-256 ed4f4bf8cba7cd73efba45ab07edec96f6173e40007d5aa1b9fb188b7bcc252d) records 3,207 source-0 entries into 0x823B37B8 and 2,746 calls to deferred consumer 0x823A4640 from guest LR 0x823B3844. This updates the earlier no-source-0 observation: the retail MMIO gate path is now taken. The sampled deferred indices stay 0/0, predicate values are 0x00/0x04/0x14 with mask 0x02 clear, and candidate producer 0x823A4758 has zero hits. The wait remains active; this does not justify fabricating the predicate or patching guest semantics. A fresh 45-second read-only GDB trace on 2026-10-25, with the exact mapped plugin SHA badeb5c4052776fafca38fd265ff8c4c6091d1165ccd1da1a1bd385587a60637, reached source-0 hit counter 411 and deferred-consumer counter 380. Software queue head/tail samples advanced 1..129/3..131, while deferred queue indices remained 0/0, global 0x831B3820 remained 0, and sampled predicate values 0x00/0x04/0x14 never set mask 0x02. Producer 0x823A4758 and callback 0x82649B68 had no hits. This reproduces the queue frontier with mapped-plugin identity but does not identify the missing producer condition. These latest exact-XEX runs are constrained to host CPU IDs 0-3 (four logical CPUs) while the guest models six Xbox CPUs. ReXGlue skips per-thread host affinity below six CPUs and emits 'Too few processor cores - scheduling will be wonky'; this may affect timing but has not been shown to cause the queue or rendering frontier. A 2026-10-25 exact-symbol NtCreateFile trace maps the missing audio.bff, drivers2.lod and cameraconfig.xml opens through retail helper 0x826EF1A0 at guest LR 0x826EF304; static callers propagate -1/-5. This does not connect the opens to the independent queue/predicate frontier. A bounded exact-XEX NtCreateFile probe found two relative shader-cache opens using RootDirectory 0xFFFFFFFD (ObDosDevices); the current VFS skips that sentinel and reports no device for the relative path. Later retail PakFiles opens follow. The trace does not prove a fatal dependency or menu/race impact. The exact-XEX thunk at 0x82BA27C0 is now included in the portable ReXGlue override set and in the Linux AMD64 build. Process 2 reported this address after an ALSA-open failure, but its raw trace was unavailable; P1 smoke opened ALSA and did not directly hit the thunk, so the report remains unverified and the retail frontend/race frontier stays open. The exact retail image contains a BINK PPC code section at 0x83064C00 and direct game-code callsites into it; ReXGlue generated and registered those Bink functions. Process 2 reported sustained reads of a valid BIKi Franchise_Ident.bik while the cutscene was active, and its local path trace confirms two file opens. The P1 GDB probe did not reach Bink before faulting at 0x823A0998, so the reported decode activity is not yet independently confirmed by a Bink-entry hit; no exact output address or texture format is established. No title-specific host Bink callback was found in the app sources. A 2026-10-25 matched run reproduced SIGBUS in Memory::Initialize while /dev/shm held 14 unreferenced xenia_memory mappings (4.7G used). After unlinking only those stale names, the same host/runtime/plugin/XEX passed memory initialization and continued for 22 seconds with repeated 24-packet submit and Copy/Convert activity; the timeout then stopped it. The old runtime left one new named mapping after termination, confirmed unreferenced and manually removed. SDK commit 58e4d4b adds unlink-after-open for private POSIX guest mappings; its patch is identical to tested commit d681228 and both focused POSIX mapping regressions pass. A Release runtime from 58e4d4b loaded with the unchanged P1 executable and plugin, mapped the guest arena, and entered retail draw/CopyConvert activity without SIGBUS; its /proc mapping was deleted while the process was alive. This bounded run still shows no main menu or race, and the fix is not yet in the app default runtime. See evidence/xbox360_linux_shm_unlink_integration_20261025.json. This does not establish menu, race, or ARM64 readiness; see evidence/xbox360_linux_shm_backing_pressure_20261025.json. A 45-second exact-XEX GDB trace with the patched shared-memory runtime and hash-identified plugin observed source-0/source-1 interrupts, an advancing retail software-ring head/tail, and repeated wait returns; the deferred record queue stayed 0/0 and producer/callback had no hits. GDB did not modify guest memory. This narrows the sampled wait path but does not prove a menu/race or explain the missing callback. The same run confirmed the local extracted PE differs from the live-memory-derived PPC ELF at 0x823A4758; use the exact live ELF evidence for static claims. See evidence/xbox360_linux_guest_queue_trace_patched_runtime_20261025.json.

X3.note: Process 2 Linux evidence reports 1,828 retail PM4 packets, two guest swaps, 48 submitted retail point-list draws, and two Vulkan frame submissions. The exact-XEX Linux/GDB run recorded 161 draw submit entries and 161 accepted source-0/sample-0 Copy/Convert entries, but the retail 1280x720 A2B10G10R10 readback has zero non-black RGB pixels (FNV-1a B161DE6EEC272325). After clearing stale ReXGlue shared-memory objects, a fresh direct Linux run reproduced the same black retail readback. A separate magenta fragment-output diagnostic produced 518,400 non-black pixels (FNV-1a DA74DA070BC0D725), confirming the diagnostic raster/presenter/readback path; it is synthetic and not retail parity. Later 3-draw batches still fail the target/scissor match against PM4_XE_SWAP. Android readback is also black. At that time, visible retail output and scene parity remained unverified; the frame-specific follow-up below records the first original splash pixels. A 30-second Linux rerun with the exact host executable from the locked P1 evidence and Process 2 PR #2161 commit 8541089b produced byte-identical black readback (FNV-1a B161DE6EEC272325); repeated 3-draw batches still reject the target/scissor match. With that exact executable/plugin pair, a synthetic magenta control read back 518,400 nonblack pixels and had no 3-draw target/scissor rejection; this confirms diagnostic draw/presenter/readback coverage only, not retail parity. A later 60-second run using P2 diagnostic plugin SHA 54348dd521b97b15be963d0b9f680172dbfb83c3ef5f2fbb979f618dc9c32aaa with debug logging and no input recorded 3,010 three-draw refresh failures. The first was draw 1 sample count 1 versus frame sample count 4; both reported surfaces share color base 0, depth base 720, color format 1, and 1280x720 extent, while pitch differs (640 for draw 0, 1280 for draw 1). No shader/resource readiness diagnostic tokens appeared before this rejection, and the raw readback remains all black. This identifies the first rejection gate for this plugin build; it does not establish the correct pitch, shader translation, frontend output, or race progress. A 30-second Linux smoke using P2 plugin SHA-256 e05ea50726caea536e25f0e3f76d052e56740bdc455fb26d0884ecab8e8adfdd emitted no unresolved diagnostics for draws 27 or 28; draw 27's prior viewport/scissor rejection is absent, and batches of five indexed draws were submitted. Only draws 0 (incomplete raster state) and 29 (unsupported target/raster state) remained unresolved. The log has 1,762 presenter submission entries and no refresh failure, but no pixel readback was captured, so visible retail output remains unverified. A new 30-second Linux smoke with Process 2 plugin SHA-256 331794ec66bb3738aa3fae2c862952aa86283267c4a2b372736e5e813d42b892 emitted no unresolved-draw diagnostics for #27/#28, while #0 remained incomplete and #25/#29 remained unsupported. It logged 1,349 presenter submission entries (1,715 reported draw packets) and one guest swap-counter increment. The first 1280x720 VK_FORMAT_A2B10G10R10_UNORM_PACK32 readback is all black (0 non-black pixels; FNV-1a B161DE6EEC272325). This confirms the current first presenter output is still black; later-frame retail parity remains unverified. A 2026-10-24 Linux capture from the exact retail XEX now verifies the original SHIFT logo/loading splash in presenter submission 10 (54,748 non-black pixels; raw SHA-256 d6c09658bc16cd14056dc605fe2300becc540f0fca77a3d3e69dfae0d52f5824). A separate submission-200 capture is entirely black (SHA-256 cd6226f8bf299d3ab51cfc10af0b585167106d7caa356e8604bfe48ad9a49de5), but used a different plugin binary, so sustained output and the cause of the difference are unresolved. A later exact-XEX frame-10 readback using selected plugin artifact SHA-256 ed4f4bf8cba7cd73efba45ab07edec96f6173e40007d5aa1b9fb188b7bcc252d is black (zero nonblack RGB pixels; SHA-256 cd6226f8bf299d3ab51cfc10af0b585167106d7caa356e8604bfe48ad9a49de5). Process 2 diagnosed that plugin run as rejecting retail sampler anisotropy=3; visible output must be rechecked after that device-feature request is enabled. This is a different plugin artifact from the earlier splash capture and does not supersede its recorded pixels. A new exact-XEX Linux AMD64 run on 2026-10-24T21:46:10Z, using P2 plugin source 261ed976362d863286d3f065440cf67a5044d8a4 and SDK fix ede359f8a93cd26cb95531a0b39ed8584aa93bb7, captures presenter submission 10 with the original SHIFT logo/loading text/progress bar (59,101 non-black pixels). Its Vulkan validation log has zero VUID/Error entries while VK_EXT_swapchain_maintenance1 is enabled with its instance prerequisites. This confirms one retail splash readback, not sustained rendering or scene parity. A 60-second exact-XEX run on the newer P2 renderer source d57598912d173ebbc46f718c52dd36ae27826b06 captured submission 200 as opaque black (0 non-black RGB pixels); because the prior visible splash used a different plugin binary, this does not establish a splash-to-black transition. Current renderer logs still report missing vertex shader control register 0x2307 and an unsupported texture-fetch descriptor. A second run using the exact same host/runtime/plugin/XEX hashes as the submission-200 black readback reproduces the original logo/loading bar at submission 10 (59,101 non-black pixels). The captures are separate launches, not a continuous transition. A bounded exact-XEX NtCreateFile probe found two relative shader-cache opens using RootDirectory 0xFFFFFFFD (ObDosDevices); the current VFS skips that sentinel and reports no device for the relative path. Later retail PakFiles opens follow. The trace does not prove a fatal dependency or menu/race impact. A fresh matched XEX/runtime/plugin run with uinput Start/A reached frame 400 and captured a list-shaped non-black panel over an otherwise black frame; this does not identify the screen, prove guest input consumption, or demonstrate the main menu/race (evidence/xbox360_linux_input_frame400_20261025.json).

X4.note: The user confirmed that the original game loading screen appeared during an earlier ReXGlue Xbox run, but its exact process/build hash was not recorded. In the current controlled Linux run, callbacks and retail Vulkan submissions occur but the readback is entirely black. Four loose-file probes for menu_background.xml failed. The big-endian index of PakFiles/Menu_Background.bff is verified: 57 bounded members include menu_background.sgx/.enx and textures, but no menu_background.xml. The misses do not prove a fatal VFS problem or show whether the game opens this archive. The main menu and offline race remain unverified; the later exact-XEX Linux splash readback is recorded in evidence/xbox360_linux_retail_splash_readback_20261024.json. A controlled 2026-10-24 filtered uinput test confirms Start/A return through retail XamInputGetState for guest user 0, but these inputs did not advance the single-draw frontend. In the same retail run, four attempts to open menu_background.xml under the instances/static scene paths returned 0xc000000f; the archive index only proves Menu_Background.bff contains SGX/ENX and texture members, not the XML or fatality of the miss. A 2026-10-25 exact-XEX caller trace now shows the resource-loader parent stores its child's result at offset 1456, sets its own return to 1, and returns on the observed path; these XML misses therefore do not directly fail that initializer. The last 14-packet draw submission preceded the first miss by about 0.75 seconds, and no further draw submission appears before this run ends; that timing is the next P1 trace point but does not establish causality. The independent 60-second GDB trace observes source-0 callbacks reaching the retail deferred consumer, but the software queue remains empty and its mask 0x02 predicate remains clear; the producer 0x823A4758 is not reached. This run still has no verified main menu or race. The new 2026-10-25 validation evidence records the same original splash readback; no main menu or offline race is demonstrated. The current plugin's submission-200 readback is opaque black; the earlier submission-10 splash came from another plugin build, so sustained frontend progress remains unverified. The mapped-plugin queue trace reproduces the source-0/deferred-consumer path without changing guest memory; its queue/predicate frontier remains open. With the same exact binaries as the separate submission-200 opaque-black run, submission 10 reproduces the original loading splash; no menu/race is shown, and the two runs do not establish a continuous transition. The current test environment exposes only four host CPUs for six guest CPUs, so ReXGlue skips per-thread host affinity and warns that scheduling may be wonky. This is a possible timing confound, not an established cause of the stall. The 2026-10-25 same-build predicate-return probe observed at least 1,792 post-call samples in 20 seconds: guest r3 was 1 in every logged sample, the software-ring head advanced from 3 toward the expected cursor, and repeated entries at 0x823A557C show that the retail wait returns as cursor values advance. This narrows the active P1 search beyond the ring-wait path; the probe still shows no menu or race, and GDB timing is intrusive. The 2026-10-25 caller trace records the cameraconfig.xml failure in the retail 0x826EF1A0 -> 0x822DD650 -> 0x822DC478 chain; missing-file sentinels propagate, but neither the trace nor BFF index proves whether the main menu or race requires archive fallback. Process 2 reports the submit-130 cutscene output as black with three fullscreen untextured zero-color draws; the saved readback is also all black. The XEX embeds Bink decode and texture integration code, so this alone does not establish a missing media callback. Main-menu and offline-race output remain unverified. Exact live-memory-derived PPC disassembly shows the traced cameraconfig.xml miss maps through the retail file-reader sentinel -5 to a false config-probe result; this path is not a proven fatal boot blocker and does not justify changing VFS semantics. The traced outer initializer cleans up associated objects and continues into later initialization; whether this config is needed in a later frontend or race state remains unknown (evidence/xbox360_linux_missing_asset_caller_semantics_20261025.json).

X5.note: No SHIFT Xbox runtime execution on target architectures

X6.note: Source audit found a Vulkan 1.1 path but three optional feature bits are hard requirements; device feature probe and retail draw/present proof are pending. A Linux host run now verifies swapchain-maintenance extension activation with the required surface prerequisites and no validation VUIDs; Vulkan 1.1-only device compatibility remains unproven.
